title: Run 3 · Batched routed-expert launches (AQBCD)
purpose: Evaluate batched routed-expert kernel launches on the released AQBC engine. Stop before a candidate build if the current backend already batches the eligible decode shapes or no eligible shape is proven.

covers: Pinned AQBC source, image and mixed pack
Dispatch eligibility before any candidate work
Conditional gated patch, deterministic fixtures, build and lab delivery
excludes: Weight, routing, gate, prefill or prompt-policy changes
A candidate build without positive dispatch evidence
Any Muse load in the factory stage

prompt_512.description: Fixed text that renders to 512 tokens with the Muse no-thinking chat template.

prompt_2048.description: Fixed text that renders to 2048 tokens with the Muse no-thinking chat template.

arms.summary: Released AQBC with pinned mixed pack, prefill plan and prompt reuse.
AQBC plus default-off gated batching of compatible routed-expert launches.

decode_tokens_per_second.how: Generated tokens after the first, over the time they took, from the server's timings.

client_ttft_ms.how: Client clock from sending the request to the first streamed token.

request_total_ms.how: Client clock from sending the request to the last streamed token (32 generated tokens).

sampled_peak_memory_bytes.how: Highest sampled resident memory of the engine process group under the cap.

device_peak_mib.how: Peak of the comparable device-budget accounting categories for the full run.

protocol.notes: Repeat seeded 512/2048 first requests and same-document follow-up pairs, comparing AQBC to AQBCD on the same target. Record startup separately and retain background activity. Within three serial capped loads total, use the third only for the off-switch control if necessary.

checks.does: Same deterministic generated tokens in AQBC, AQBCD with batching on and AQBCD with batching off.
Record comparable restored token counts for both same-document lengths with reuse enabled.
Show the off switch reaches the original implementation and agrees with AQBC under the same workload.

rules: If the pinned AQBC backend already batches eligible shapes or no eligible shape is proven, halt before any candidate build, retain the native trace and leave AQBC released.

On the same target and seeded workloads, require repeatable AQBCD decode improvement beyond repeat variation, identical generated tokens, unchanged prefix reuse, at most 10% first-token and total latency regression, and compliance with both memory caps.
By Nov 29 18:00 ET, publish the lab verdict if the candidate qualified and was delivered; absent acceptance leave AQBC released.

execution.notes: Factory stage never loads Muse. Only the independent lab after an accepted delivery may run up to three serial owner-gated capped loads under 96 GiB with no swap; 110000 MiB device budget and one model at a time.

notes: Owner 018 selects candidate 1 and supersedes withdrawn 012.
The released AQBC image and the native release receipt are pinned by the operator parent reference.

outputs.name: dispatch_trace
criteria: Trace the pinned compiled backend and visited routing paths for both AQBC quantized expert formats. Seal eligibility and may_build. A confirmed already-batched or no-eligible-shape result satisfies this check and stops the project before candidate work.

After the check passes read its sealed dispatch_trace, mark the node done citing the accepted node_check. With may_build false, do not patch, build, deliver or load. Publish native stop_missing_prerequisite citing the accepted trace_dispatch node_check observation ID and give the exact eligibility as action.eligibility. Explain the observed stop reason in action.reason.

criteria: Check repeated experts, unequal gates, partial tiles, both AQBC formats, all routes exactly once, independent original-path output and off-switch behavior using small fixtures without Muse.
